title: Sebastian and the Will
premise: True-crime podcaster Rosalind Ravensworth inherits the unsolved 1974 disappearance of Elowen Marsh, a lighthouse keeper's daughter who vanished from the Cornish coast, and discovers Elowen's diary contains entries written after her supposed death. Following the diary's coded references to a smugglers' tunnel beneath the Ravensworth family's own estate, Rosalind uncovers that Elowen faked her drowning to escape an arranged marriage and a complicit village, living out her days in hiding as the town's beloved postmistress. In the climax, Rosalind confronts the last living conspirator—her own grandmother—and must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy her family or honoring the woman who chose love over duty; she broadcasts the story but lets the tide keep the body, finally giving both women the belonging they were denied.
about_author: Hazel Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing cold-case files in coastal England before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about small towns that keep their secrets the way the sea keeps its dead.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case on Record
chapters.summary: Rosalind Ravensworth, mid-production slump on her true-crime podcast, receives a battered diary from a solicitor handling her late aunt's estate: the 1974 case of missing Elowen Marsh. Flipping through it in her London flat, she finds entries dated weeks after the disappearance. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: restless curiosity sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Ink Past the End
chapters.summary: Rosalind verifies the handwriting against museum samples of Elowen's letters—the post-disappearance entries are authentic. The final entry reads only 'the tide keeps what it is given.' She books a train to Cornwall over her producer's objections. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the thrill of a story no one else can tell.

chapters.title: Saltburn Point
chapters.summary: Arriving in the decaying fishing village, Rosalind finds a community that treats Elowen's disappearance as sacred ground not to be disturbed. The pub goes quiet when she mentions the name. An old fisherman warns her off with strange gentleness. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the first taste of a town closing ranks.

chapters.title: What the Lighthouse Saw
chapters.summary: Rosalind interviews retired keeper Thomas Penhale, who was sixteen in 1974 and swears he saw Elowen walk toward the cliff path alone—but never saw her reach the edge. His account contradicts the official drowning verdict. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: doubt taking root in the official record.

chapters.title: A Diary That Keeps Writing
chapters.summary: Back at her rented cottage, Rosalind decodes the later diary entries: references to a 'green door,' a borrowed name, and someone called only 'S.' The entries are tender, domestic, alive. She realizes Elowen didn't just survive—she built a life. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: awe replacing grief.

chapters.title: The Postmistress
chapters.summary: Rosalind cross-references village records and discovers that 'Edith Voss,' the beloved postmistress who died in 2019, arrived in Saltburn Point three months after Elowen vanished—with no history before her. The villagers' reverence suddenly reads differently. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a hidden life in plain sight.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: In the post office archive, Rosalind finds a drawer of undelivered letters Edith wrote to 'S' over forty years—love letters, patient and aching. Whoever S was, they stayed nearby all along. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: tenderness complicating the investigation.

chapters.title: Grandmother Knows Best
chapters.summary: Rosalind visits her grandmother Vivienne Ravensworth, whose family estate borders the Marsh land, ostensibly for tea. Vivienne deflects every question about 1974 with polished charm, but her hands shake when Rosalind mentions the green door. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: suspicion arriving somewhere it doesn't belong.

chapters.title: The Arranged Match
chapters.summary: Digging into parish records, Rosalind learns Elowen was betrothed in 1974—to Rosalind's grandfather, Charles Ravensworth, a merger of two struggling families. The diary's fear of 'the wedding' reframes everything. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: her own family implicated in the escape.

chapters.title: S Is for Sebastian
chapters.summary: Rosalind finds the green door: a sealed cellar entrance on the Ravensworth estate leading to the old smugglers' tunnel network. Carved inside, initials entwined: E.M. and S.R.—Sebastian Ravensworth, Charles's younger brother, presumed drowned himself in 1975. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the love story surfacing from stone.

chapters.title: Two Drownings, One Lie
chapters.summary: Rosalind reconstructs the plan: Sebastian staged his own death a year later to join Elowen in hiding, and the families buried both scandals quietly. But someone had to organize the cover-up—and keep it buried for fifty years. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: anger hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Producer's Warning
chapters.summary: Her producer arrives unannounced, urging Rosalind to drop it: the podcast survives on strangers' tragedies, not her own bloodline. They fight. Alone afterward, Rosalind admits the case has stopped being content and become personal. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the cost of knowing named aloud.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Version
chapters.summary: Rosalind confronts Vivienne directly. Her grandmother admits she found the lovers' plan in 1974 and said nothing—not from kindness, but because Elowen's flight freed Charles to marry wealth elsewhere. 'I kept our secret,' she says. 'You'll keep ours.' POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: blackmail dressed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Someone Else Is Listening
chapters.summary: Rosalind notices she's being followed—a grey Rover appears at the archive, outside the cottage, on the cliff road. Someone else has connected Edith Voss to Elowen Marsh, and they want the story silenced before broadcast. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: The Heir
chapters.summary: Rosalind identifies her tail: Julian Ravensworth, a cousin managing the family trust, whose fortune depends on the estate's clean title—which a reopened inquest could cloud. He offers her money to kill the episode. She refuses. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: duty versus truth made literal.

chapters.title: Down the Smugglers' Run
chapters.summary: Followed into the tunnels during a storm, Rosalind uses the diary's coded route descriptions to evade Julian and reaches a hidden chamber: two chairs, a tin of letters, and evidence Sebastian lived there until 1981, when he died in Elowen's arms. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: standing inside a whole hidden marriage.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Among the chamber's papers is Elowen's true final entry, describing Sebastian's death and her choice to return to the village as Edith rather than grieve alone—choosing proximity to his memory over freedom. Rosalind weeps for a woman she never met. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: grief inherited across generations.

chapters.title: Julian at the Door
chapters.summary: Julian corners Rosalind at the cottage, demanding the diary and tapes, escalating to threats. Thomas Penhale intervenes—it emerges he helped the lovers escape as a boy and has guarded the secret ever since. The old allies of the lie divide anew. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: courage borrowed from the faithful dead.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Rosalind releases the full season: the arranged marriage, the faked drownings, the forty-year love affair, and the cover-up—naming Vivienne and Julian but framing them within Elowen's agency, not as villains of it. The internet ignites; the family trust begins to fracture. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the point of no return, embraced.

chapters.title: The Confrontation at Ravensworth Hall
chapters.summary: Climax: Vivienne summons Rosalind to the hall and reveals one last card—proof that exposing everything could legally unravel Rosalind's own inheritance too. Mother-figure against granddaughter, each holding a knife wrapped in love. Rosalind chooses truth anyway, telling her grandmother some stories aren't hers to bury. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Resolution begins: the coroner formally reopens and closes the case—Elowen Marsh died in 2020 as Edith Voss, loved and mourned twice. Julian resigns under pressure; Vivienne, stripped of leverage, sends Rosalind Elowen's wedding ring, found in a drawer decades ago. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning, no absolution asked.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Will
chapters.summary: On the cliff above the tunnel mouth, Rosalind records the season finale, reading Elowen's last entry aloud to the sea. She buries the ring beside the green door and understands at last why the diary kept writing: a life isn't closed just because a file is. She walks home through the village that finally knows her. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: belonging earned, memory honored, love outlasting duty.
